title: Leadership All-Hands — Q2 Kickoff & Strategy
summary: Company-wide Q2 kickoff: CEO overview of business priorities, CTO & VP Eng technical updates, Product roadmap highlights, CFO financial targets and hiring pause discussion, HR updates on benefits and hybrid policy. Q&A covered Dedicated vs Private customer requests, SOC2 timelines, and next steps for town halls and team OKRs.
next_steps: Leadership to share updated Q2 OKRs doc by 2025-04-11
Eng teams to review proposed latency targets and report back by 2025-04-18
Security to share SOC2 gap analysis and remediation plan by 2025-04-30
People Ops to schedule benefits Q&A session by 2025-04-16
action_items: Maya Patel: Draft runtime performance roadmap — due 2025-04-18
Carlos Romero: Update revenue forecast & hiring spend — due 2025-04-11
Priya Shah: Publish product launch checklist for Redwood Optimize — due 2025-04-14
transcript:
[00:00] Moderator - Alex: Good morning everyone, welcome to the Q2 leadership all-hands. We'll kick off in about 30 seconds. Please keep mics muted unless you're speaking.
[00:27] Ethan Brooks (CEO): Hey team, uh, thanks for joining. Happy Q2 — wow, okay, deep breath. I wanted to start with a quick status, high level numbers, then we'll move to product and ops. We closed the quarter, we beat ARR target by about 4%, which is great but margin is tight, and we have a lot of work to get to the unit economics we want.
[01:05] Ethan: Big thank you to sales and solutions for the redwood dedicated deals, and engineering for the late-night deploys on the runtime. A couple of themes for Q2: reliability first, tighten cost per token, and accelerate private deployments.
[01:32] Maya Patel (CTO): Yeah, and on that point — reliability first — the infra team has been focused on two things: kernel selection optimizations and KV cache stability. We saw a persistent regression in the KV cash, um, cache, that caused tail latency spikes in late March.
[01:58] Luis Navarro (VP Eng): Just to be clear, the root cause was a miss-ordered checkpoint during autoscaling; when nodes scaled down, some cache state wasn't rehydrated fast enough. We patched it, and metric SLOs have improved but we want to validate across more traffic.
[02:25] Priya Shah (Head of Product): On product, Q2 roadmap emphasizes Redwood Console enhancements: token-level costing per route, a new rollout UI for canary/AB, and deeper observability into model rollouts. We're planning a beta for select customers mid-May.
[02:48] Ethan: Helpful to call out customer asks — several of them want private VPC deployments with HSM-level key control, so that's high on the priority list.
[03:05] Jenna Li (Head of People): Quick HR update: no major changes to benefits, but we are pausing external hiring for non-critical roles for the next 30 days while finance and leadership recalibrate forecast. Internal mobility remains open. We'll host a live Q&A next week.
[03:30] Carlos Romero (CFO): On finances: revenue was slightly ahead, but gross margin compression due to GPU spot pricing and higher networking egress costs. We're targeting a 15% reduction in variable infra spend via more aggressive quantization guidance and smarter routing policies.
[03:58] Ethan: I also want to highlight customer reliability — we had one incident where a regional outage led to failover issues; thanks to the on-call for handling it. Postmortem will be posted with action items.
[04:20] Moderator - Alex: Quick housekeeping: recording is enabled; if you ask a question in chat we'll try to surface it during the Q&A.
[04:36] Attendee - Samir Kaur: Question for Maya — can you clarify the KV cache patch and whether it affects Dedicated customers on reserved capacity?
[04:50] Maya: Great question. The patch is orthogonal to allocation mode; Dedicated pools rely on the same runtime, but Dedicated has stricter autoscale rules so the particular scale-down pattern that triggered the bug was mostly seen in hosted burst scenarios. We will verify Dedicated pools separately.
[05:15] Luis: We're also adding a simulation harness to reproduce autoscale churn so we can test rehydration flows without hitting prod.
[05:29] Attendee - Nina Park (Product Marketing): Any update on the Redwood Optimize public launch timeline?
[05:37] Priya: We're targeting an internal launch late April for a small set of pilot customers, with broader org availability mid-June. The initial feature set is batching/caching suggestions, quantization recommendations, and cost impact visualizations.
[05:55] Ethan: Important note: initial pilots will include a small number of customers; we want performance and cost numbers to be rock-solid before public messaging.
[06:10] Attendee - Toby Evans (Security Eng): SOC2 question — where are we on the audit readiness checklist?
[06:18] Carlos: Security team completed the first gap analysis; major items are formalized IAM controls, audit log retention policy, and key management documentation. We're aiming to submit the readiness package to auditors by end of Q2.
[06:37] Maya: There's also a small infra ask for KMS integration in the private agent. It's on the infra backlog but we need to prioritize.
[06:48] Ethan: OK, switching gears to product metrics — Priya, could you walk through the model adoption numbers?
[06:56] Priya: Sure — top-line, usage of our curated open models grew 22% QoQ, embeddings usage is up 40% due to a few search and retrieval pilots, but per-customer token counts vary widely. We're focusing on higher-value customers for private deployments which drives steady MRR.
[07:20] Priya: Also want to call out the eval team: they found a subtle regression in structured outputs for one model family after a quantization change — that triggered our new regression alert flow and prevented a bad rollout.
[07:38] Ethan: Love that. Ops folks, that's exactly the kind of guardrail we need.
[07:45] Attendee - Amir Saleh: On Dedicated pricing — are we revisiting commit levels vs burst capacity? Customers ask about predictable throughput but also want headroom.
[07:56] Carlos: We're testing new tiering: base reserved capacity plus a burst pool priced separately. Economics modeled in the spreadsheet we'll share after the all-hands.
[08:12] Ethan: We'll post that spreadsheet. Action for finance to annotate the assumptions.
[08:20] Attendee - Samir: Any update on region expansion? APAC asks are increasing.
[08:26] Luis: We're prioritizing a single APAC region in partnership with a cloud provider; timeline is mid-Q3 due to capacity constraints. We'll offer private deployments with local egress controls.
[08:41] Moderator - Alex: Quick poll in chat — are there questions in the queue?
[08:48] Attendee - Multiple (chat): Lots of questions about hiring, the hiring pause, the budget, and the product roadmap.
[08:58] Ethan: On hiring — it's a pause for non-critical roles. If your team has a critical need, please escalate to leadership with a one-pager and spend justification.
[09:12] Jenna: We'll provide a template for justifications.
[09:18] Attendee - Samir: Follow-up on SSO/SAML for Private customers, timeline?
[09:24] Maya: SSO improvements are in progress, the early adopter private package will have SAML and basic RBAC, full enterprise SSO integration slated post-beta.
[09:36] Carlos: Funding note — the Series C has runway to cover planned expansions but we need to tighten spend to hit a couple of milestones that unlock the next tranche.
[09:50] Ethan: We need to be very deliberate with hiring and product bets.
[10:00] Attendee - Priya (interjects): Sorry — quick product note: we want to run a canary of the new rollout UI with the Platform team next Tuesday.
[10:07] Luis: I'll assign eng owners and set up the canary.
[10:12] Attendee - Nina: Marketing note — we'll need feature copy and timing for the Redwood Console beta. Priya, can the PM team sync with us today?
[10:20] Priya: Yes.
[10:22] [11:00] Ethan: Alright let's jump to a short demo from Maya on the latency improvements and a chart — Maya?
[11:10] Maya: Quick share — sorry the slide deck link is in chat. The main change was switching the attention kernel for long sequences which reduced 99th percentile latency by about 18% on average workloads. We also tuned the continuous batching thresholds to avoid stranding small requests.
[11:37] Maya: There is a tradeoff with batching and tail latency; smart routing will help us pick routing policies per customer SLOs.
[11:48] Attendee - Samir: Was there any user-facing regression after the kernel change?
[11:52] Maya: No. We rolled it to a small subset and monitored evals. There was a mismatch in one of the model configs but we rolled a fix quickly.
[12:04] Attendee - Carlos: Question on billing — will standing committed capacity be billed differently if we introduce burst pools?
[12:13] Carlos: Yes billing will reflect base commitments and separate burst usage; more detailed model coming in the spreadsheet.
[12:20] Attendee - Toby: Can we make sure audit logs for Private deployments have separate retention tiers? This is a customer ask for compliance.
[12:31] Maya: Yep, that's in scope for the Private package. We'll document retention and export APIs.
[12:40] Attendee - Amir: Anything new on partner integrations?
[12:44] Ethan: We're exploring a couple of partnerships for the APAC region and a GPU vendor to secure capacity. We have an NDA in flight with a cloud partner.
[12:55] [13:00] Q&A segment continues with mixed chat and mics: several employees ask about bonuses, comp cycle, roadmap specifics. HR and Finance confirm compensation review is scheduled for Q3.
[13:35] Ethan: On bonuses and comp — no immediate changes, but we are looking at variable bonus structure tied to reliability and cost metrics. More detail in the compensation town hall.
[13:50] Attendee - Multiple: applause emoji in chat.
[14:00] Priya: Quick product highlight — Redwood Optimize pilot success story: a pilot customer reduced per-token cost by 27% while keeping latency targets. We'll publish a short case study.
[14:20] Attendee - Nina: We'll need customer approval for the case study.
[14:26] Priya: We'll coordinate with Solutions and Legal.
[14:32] [20:00] (transcription drift — some speakers overlapped in chat)
[20:25] Luis: Engineering note — we're increasing observability retention for model rollout traces to 90 days to better support incident investigations; cost impact is small compared to the benefit.
[20:40] Attendee - Samir: Will that impact SLO dashboards?
[20:45] Luis: Shouldn't, dashboards will aggregate as before.
[20:50] [25:00] Ethan: Final topics — org structure tweaks: small consolidation in infra team, moving Platform into Core Infra, and a new Director of Reliability role. More details later this week.
[25:30] Jenna: We'll post org chart and open office hours for questions.
[25:45] Attendee - Amir: Any heads-up on layoffs?
[25:50] Ethan: No. We're doing a hiring pause for non-essential roles, but no layoffs planned. We'll be transparent.
[26:05] Q&A winds down; chat questions waived.
[26:20] Ethan: Quick recap and explicit next steps. Leadership will publish updated OKRs, finance will send the annotated budget spreadsheet, security posts SOC2 plan, People Ops schedules the hiring Q&A.
[26:40] Moderator - Alex: Thank you everyone; we will record and share. Closing in 30 seconds.
[26:50] Attendee - Multiple: thank you, bye.
[27:00] (meeting ends early)
Note: Transcript contains automatic captions and some mis-hearings (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', 'H S M' vs 'HSM'). Post-meeting docs: slides deck link in chat, budget spreadsheet link to be shared, postmortem link pending.
